model_description: COMPLIANT modular-multiplication scratchpad. Takes RAW (a, b, p) with NO a%p/b%p preprocessing and does the whole task in-network, per the organizer ruling (input must be raw; the reduction of the large operand mod p is the intended core). One learned per-step primitive cell(acc, m, digit) = (acc*10 + m*digit) mod p, applied in two phases on a fixed schedule: Phase 1 reduces a mod p (Horner over a's raw digits, m=1) -> a_red; Phase 2 multiplies over b's raw digits with m=a_red -> (a*b) mod p. The answer is the model's own final generated acc (base conversion only in the harness). Fixed input schedule + learned steps => compliant; randomising the weights collapses accuracy. Sized for tiers 1-3 (raw operands up to 64 bits ~20 digits, p < 2^16); emits 0 for p>=10^5 or operand>=10^20. Verified arithmetically exact over 36k raw-operand cases.
training_description: Trained from scratch (raw vocab/two-phase layout; no warm-start from the reduced-operand models) on tiers 1-3 with a held-out prime split, RAW operands sampled up to each tier's operand_bits (dev/data.py OPERAND_BITS; --raw-operands), and an operand-magnitude curriculum that grows a,b from 1 to 20 digits so the reduction is bootstrapped. The remaining wall is rollout drift over the ~730-token two-phase scratchpad; the drift lever is on-policy training (--sched-samp), a one-flag hardening pass after the operation is learned. Compliant: worked steps are training targets, answer is the model's generated acc (collapses under weight perturbation), no hand-coded arithmetic, no external controller. See dev/train_recurrent.py (make_batch_raw + exact_match op_bound).
